convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom for MACD_Xtr indicator and includes TradeAlgorithms.mqh for position management, both of which require manual recreation in Python

other_exits: Close long when MACD_Xtr signal==0 (sell signal) with SellPosClose permission
Close short when MACD_Xtr signal==2 (buy signal) with BuyPosClose permission
Close both long and short when MACD_Xtr signal==1 (no trend) with respective close permissions

position_sizing.conditional_logic: negative MM value = fixed lot size (abs value), positive MM value = deposit fraction for deal sizing

custom_logic_notes: Entry uses MACD_Xtr custom indicator buffer 1 with discrete signal values: 0=bearish, 1=no trend, 2=bullish. Buy signal requires Signal[1]==2 AND Signal[0]!=2 (trend just turned bullish on previous bar, not current). Sell signal requires Signal[1]==0 AND Signal[0]!=0. Signal[1]==1 (no trend) triggers close on both sides. Additional entry gate: Signal[0] must differ from Signal[1] to confirm a fresh signal change. BuyPosOpen/SellPosOpen/SellPosClose/BuyPosClose booleans act as permission gates for each direction. Recount flag triggers recalculation if data copy fails. If SignalBar==0, intrabar recalculation is allowed bypassing new-bar guard.
python_conversion_notes: Must recreate MACD_Xtr custom indicator logic in Python. The indicator uses a damped/smoothed MACD with volatility weighting (xVolatility) and source selection (ATR/StDev/Volume). TradeAlgorithms.mqh provides BuyPositionOpen/SellPositionOpen/BuyPositionClose/SellPositionClose - need to reimplement these with position checking, lot sizing from MM parameter (negative=fixed lots, positive=deposit fraction), and SL/TP in points. The signal logic is discrete (0,1,2) rather than crossover-based, simplifying entry detection. No digit adjustment needed - SL/TP are in points directly. The CIsNewBar class and LoadHistory function need Python equivalents for bar-level timing.
